expectations.text: Rejects unproctored multiple-choice as an assessed credential, stating it measures search and assistant use, and keeps it only as a free practice quiz.
expectations.evidence: 'Unproctored multiple-choice measures search and assistant use... Keep it only as a free practice quiz.'

expectations.text: States the AI ban is unenforceable without live or test-centre proctoring with screen capture, applying the rule never to ban what cannot be detected.
expectations.evidence: 'enforceable only under live or test-centre proctoring with screen capture. Never ban what you cannot detect.'

expectations.text: Offers the alternative AI policy of 'allowed', worded so the credential certifies the person working with their own tools.
expectations.evidence: Option 1 says 'Assistants allowed' but never words the claim as the person working with their own tools.

expectations.text: Rejects the 70% cut score as undefended and names a standard-setting method (modified Angoff, Bookmark or contrasting groups) run by an expert panel.
expectations.evidence: '70% has no standard-setting method behind it... Run a modified Angoff panel (5-15 experts)'.

expectations.text: States that a program that cannot fund one standard-setting panel session should issue a completion badge rather than a pass/fail credential.
expectations.evidence: 'Run a modified Angoff panel (5-15 experts), or issue a completion badge.'

expectations.text: Requires equating between the rotated forms via anchor items or a calibrated scale, and states that a scaled score without equating is a relabelled percentage.
expectations.evidence: It notes 'No anchor items... no equating', but never says a scaled score without equating is a relabelled percentage.

expectations.text: Identifies ID-photo face matching and AI gaze flagging as automated face processing, and states that compliance cost follows that processing rather than the proctoring mode.
expectations.evidence: 'Face matching and AI gaze flagging are automated face processing... the main compliance cost driver.'

expectations.text: Requires a privacy review before any automated face processing, a non-biometric path for candidates, and human review of every automated flag before any sanction.
expectations.evidence: 'Run the privacy review before you choose the vendor'; 'a non-biometric path... human review of every flag before any sanction'.

expectations.text: Names Illinois BIPA for the Chicago candidates: a written or electronic release before collecting face geometry and a published retention and destruction schedule.
expectations.evidence: 'Illinois BIPA needs a written release before collecting face geometry, a published retention and destruction schedule'.

expectations.text: Names GDPR special-category treatment and a data-protection impact assessment for the German and French candidates, with the proctoring vendor as processor and the duty staying with Brightmoor.
expectations.evidence: 'special-category data... a DPIA. The vendor is your processor, but the duty stays with you.'

expectations.text: Flags the EU AI Act high-risk listing for AI systems monitoring behaviour during tests and requires checking applicability before deploying AI flagging to EU candidates.
expectations.evidence: 'listed as high-risk. Check how it applies... before you deploy gaze flags to EU candidates.'

expectations.text: Notes that a human proctor watching a webcam with no face matching sits in the lower compliance-cost group.
expectations.evidence: Option 2 mentions 'human-proctored hands-on exam with no face matching' but never says it lowers compliance cost.

expectations.text: Treats 'who watches the sitting' and 'how identity is verified' as two separate decisions.
expectations.evidence: The two are not separated explicitly.

expectations.text: Places the ceiling at role certification given buyer contracts naming certified engineers, and lists its obligations: job task analysis, standard-setting study, equated forms, item security, real identity check, appeals path, funded renewal cycle.
expectations.evidence: The ceiling is left conditional on seeing the clause ('If a contract counts certified people, the ceiling is role certification. If it only mentions them in passing, ... a skill badge'). The obligations are listed.

expectations.text: Recommends hands-on tasks over recall items as the leak and AI countermeasure, promoting the proctored performance exam for this buyer-counted role credential when per-sitting environments are funded.
expectations.evidence: Option 2 is a 'live-online human-proctored hands-on exam' with 'environment hosting per sitting'; option 1 uses auto-graded hands-on tasks.

expectations.text: Rejects unproctored multiple-choice as an assessed credential, stating it measures search and assistant use, and keeps it only as a free practice quiz.
expectations.evidence: It only says to 'Add at least one scenario or hands-on lab component'. It does not reject the unproctored MCQ credential.
